import sys, json, re, datetime

# The three kinds a fact may be, byte-identical to `extract-glue`'s: an
# annotation naming anything else is dropped THERE, so it is dropped here --
# where the drop can still be counted instead of vanishing one lane later.
KINDS = ("world", "experience", "foresight")

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
# This cell's OWN configuration arrives on the same stdin document: `params` is
# one of its three top-level objects, beside `envelope` and `body`, and the
# substrate always sets it ({} when there is nothing to hand over). Every knob
# below is read from it, so each one is per-INSTANCE configuration -- two
# members of one colony have their memories tuned apart, and a mutation retunes
# one of them without touching a colony-wide environment (GH #138). The literal
# beside each name is the shipped default; it is the same value the template
# config and `contract.settings` carry, and a test pins the three against each
# other.
P = doc.get("params") or {}


def _knob(key, default):
    # A knob explicitly set to null or to whitespace is "not configured", not a
    # crash: an operator who blanks a line in a config means the default. Both
    # knobs of this cell are numbers, and `_int` below is where the blank string
    # is turned back into the default -- there is no number in it to read.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    return default if v is None else v


def _int(key, default):
    v = _knob(key, default)
    if isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip():
        return default
    return int(v)


def _data(key, default):
    # A block of DATA (the language grammar of a forget request): an object as
    # configured, the default where it is missing or not an object. No literal
    # copy of it lives in the script -- the data has one home, the params.
    v = _knob(key, default)
    return v if isinstance(v, dict) else default


def _flag(key, default):
    # A switch. On is true, "true", 1 or "1"; off is false, "false", 0 or "0";
    # a blanked line or null is the default. Anything else is a typo, said in
    # the journal with the knob's name, and the default holds: a switch that
    # read a typo silently would leave the operator believing it is on.
    v = P.get(key, default)
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, str) and not v.strip()):
        return default
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return v
    if isinstance(v, int) and v in (0, 1):
        return v == 1
    if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip().lower() in ("true", "1", "false", "0"):
        return v.strip().lower() in ("true", "1")
    # Review KF-F (NIT): a stop here took the whole lane with it, the session
    # close included.
    sys.stderr.write("close-glue: %s is a switch -- true or false (also 1/0), not %s; "
                     "the default %s holds\n" % (key, json.dumps(v)[:40], json.dumps(default)))
    return default


d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {})
phase = str(ctx.get("mem_phase", ""))
op = hop.get("operation")
# GH #343: `operation` says WHICH op answered, `error_code` says WHETHER it
# worked. Since GH #331 a store refusal stamps BOTH, so a failure now arrives
# looking exactly like an answer and both fields have to be read.
err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")
# The session IS the identity of this pass -- there is no run id of its own. A
# session closes once, and the turns of that session are exactly the material
# the pass reads, so a second key would only be a second way to disagree with
# the first. It travels as ingress context and the lane DECLARES it, which is
# what makes the guard below a park rather than a refusal: a caller who never
# promoted it is refused at mutation time, so a hop that arrives here without
# one is a stray echo, not a request.
session_id = str(ctx.get("session_id", "") or "")
# #244 / ADR-0002 E2: the room and the cast of the closing session are NOT
# bound here, and that is the decision rather than an omission. Context is
# CARRIED: the substrate hands an envelope's context on across every hop a cell
# emits, so both keys reach the ingress on the write blocks below without this
# lane copying them -- and what the ingress finally writes inherits one
# dimension further on, from the EPISODE each fact hangs on (E12: provenance is
# recorded once and never rewritten). A copy read here would be a second source
# for a value nobody has to copy, and the only thing a second source can do is
# disagree.
# Page bound of the session read. Ordered NEWEST first on purpose: a session
# longer than one page loses its oldest turns rather than its last ones, and the
# later a turn is, the more likely it is the one that corrects an earlier -- the
# whole reason this pass exists. The page is re-ordered oldest-first before it
# reaches a prompt: the ORDER OF THE READ decides which turns survive the bound,
# the order of the RENDERING is the prompt phase's business and not this one's.
TURN_ROWS = _int("close_turn_rows", 512)
# Page bound of the fact read, one dimension over: a session has turns, and the
# facts those turns left standing are a different count entirely -- a short
# session can carry a long history if its subject has been talked about before.
FACT_ROWS = _int("close_fact_rows", 256)
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def park():
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def emit(msgs):
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(msgs))
    sys.exit(0)


def store_op(args, ph):
    return {"header": {"route": "cstore", "phase": ph},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "c-" + ph,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)}]}


def store_bundle(calls, ph):
    """GH #295: N ops in ONE message, answered in ONE reply (`operation`
    "bundle", one `tool_result` turn per op, correlated by its id). R-TR-25,
    kfm M1b: the mute reads and their park ride the exceptions read and its
    park this way -- as three stations of their own they cost the close lane
    six routing decisions, 53 of the 48 its budget allows (gh933 (f))."""
    return {"header": {"route": "cstore", "phase": ph},
            "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                          "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in calls]}


def legs_of(doc):
    """The rows of each op of a bundle reply, by its tool_call id."""
    out = {}
    for m in doc.get("messages") or []:
        if not isinstance(m, dict):
            continue
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m.get("text") or "[]")
        except Exception:
            payload = []
        out[str(m.get("id") or "")] = payload if isinstance(payload, list) else []
    return out


def rows_of(doc):
    msgs = doc.get("messages", [])
    if not msgs:
        return []
    try:
        payload = json.loads(msgs[0].get("text", "[]"))
    except Exception:
        return []
    return payload if isinstance(payload, list) else []


def first_text(doc):
    for m in doc.get("messages", []):
        if m.get("type") in ("text", "tool_result") and m.get("text"):
            return m.get("text")
    return ""


# GH #343: a store refusal is not a result. `op` is what says "this came from
# the store": nothing else that reaches this cell stamps it. So a hop carrying
# BOTH op and error_code is a refusal, and a refusal is TERMINAL -- the chain
# stops here, no further store op leaves, and the failure is SAID on the reject
# lane the hive declares for exactly this. It stands ABOVE the session guard for
# the same reason it does in dream-glue: a store reply whose context lost the
# session key is still a store reply saying a read did not happen, and parking
# it swallows exactly the news worth having.
# A bundle (GH #295) is not a transaction and stamps no `error_code` of its
# own: it counts its refused ops in `bundle_errors` and names each one's code
# in `results[]`. One refused op is a read or a park that did not happen --
# the same terminal refusal.
#
# kfm M1c (review 5): one kind of op is NOT terminal -- the upgrade of an older
# store (`c-mute-up` and its conversions `c-mute-up-<n>`, below). A refused
# conversion stopped every close pass of the colony at the meeting, so its
# memory never closed a session again over a write the pass does not need: the
# closures stay what they were, the pass goes on, and the refusal is reported
# (`close_report` phase `mute-up`, `mute_up_refused`); the next pass tries again.
# A refused read or park of the lane's own sets stays terminal.
UPGRADE_REFUSED = []
if op == "bundle" and int(hop.get("bundle_errors") or 0):
    _refused = [r for r in (d.get("results") or [])
                if isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("error_code")]
    if _refused and all(str(r.get("tool_call_id") or "").startswith("c-mute-up")
                        for r in _refused):
        UPGRADE_REFUSED = _refused
    else:
        _bad = _refused[0] if _refused else {}
        err = str(_bad.get("error_code") or "bundle_error")
        op = "bundle " + str(_bad.get("operation") or "op")

if err and op:
    emit([{"header": {"route": "reject", "phase": "close",
                      "reject_reason": "store_refused",
                      "store_error": err, "store_operation": str(op)},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "c-reject",
                         "text": "the close pass stopped in phase '%s': the store refused"
                                 " the %s with %s (%s). Nothing the turns of this session"
                                 " already wrote was touched"
                                 % (phase, op, err, first_text(d))}]}])

if not session_id:
    park()

# ------------------------------------------------------------ park and meet
# A `code` cell is stateless and holds exactly ONE store result set at a time,
# so the four reads below cannot be compared to each other while they travel --
# they have to meet inside a table first. That is `extract-glue`'s surviving
# `dedup` -> `known` -> `merge` -> `apply` chain, and this lane uses it
# unchanged: park the answer, ask the next question, read all four back at the
# end.
#
# The key is the SESSION, not a run id of its own -- the same reason there is no
# run id anywhere else in this lane (see the note above): a session closes once,
# and a second key would only be a second way to disagree with the first.
SCRATCH_KEY = "close:" + session_id
# W4 (ruling Q2 option C), one author over: <author>:<key of the row that
# carries the reason>, the rule `extract:<batch>` and `judge:<run>` already
# follow. Here that key IS the scratch key -- the verdict this pass acted on is
# parked under it -- so a topic closed by a close pass reads back to the pass
# that closed it, and one pass is reverted with one `where`. The `close:` prefix
# is what lets the night tell the two authors apart: ruling Q9 separates the
# ROLES (session-scoped sharpening vs store-wide consolidation), not the
# policies, so `dream-glue` reviews both.
CLOSURE_SOURCE = SCRATCH_KEY
# Every read is asked for `bound + 1` rows and parks at most `bound`. A page
# that comes back exactly full is indistinguishable from a session that happens
# to end there, and `hop.truncated` in the close report has to be EXACT rather
# than probable: the extra row is the proof, it never reaches a prompt, and its
# presence is the whole flag. The cost is one row per read; the alternative --
# reporting truncation whenever `len(rows) == bound` -- calls every exactly-full
# session truncated, which is the one wrong answer nobody can distinguish from
# the right one afterwards.
PROOF = 1
# Bound of the meeting read: six kinds (the five result sets and a verdict)
# times four runs of one session, so a session closed a second time still finds
# its OWN newest row of every kind at the head of the answer. GH #933: a run
# parks one verdict PER GROUP, so the read after the verdict of group g asks for
# MEET_ROWS + g -- this run's five sets and its g + 1 verdicts are the newest
# rows under the key, and the bound keeps the same slack for earlier runs.
MEET_ROWS = 24


def park_args(kind, rows, bound):
    """The insert that parks one result set under this pass's key."""
    payload = {"rows": rows[:bound], "truncated": len(rows) > bound}
    return {"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch",
            "row": {"key": SCRATCH_KEY, "kind": kind, "created_at": now,
                    "payload": json.dumps(payload)}}


def park_rows(kind, bound, nxt):
    """Park one result set under this pass's key and ask the next question."""
    rows = rows_of(d)
    payload = {"rows": rows[:bound], "truncated": len(rows) > bound}
    row = {"key": SCRATCH_KEY, "kind": kind, "created_at": now,
           "payload": json.dumps(payload)}
    # SEQUENTIAL, not parallel -- `extract-glue` measured what a fan-out costs
    # here: two reads issued side by side both land in `scratch` and both look
    # like the last one, so the phase that meets them runs twice. One chain, one
    # meeting.
    return store_op({"operation": "insert", "table": "scratch", "row": row}, nxt)


# Deliberately NOT read: `entities`, `entity_edges`, `beliefs`, `embeddings`.
# They hang off the facts that ARE read, and none of the four points of the
# contract asks the closer to touch them -- it adds what is missing, supersedes
# what it names, sharpens what it points at and restates nothing. Written down
# so the omission is a decision on the record rather than an oversight the next
# reader has to re-derive from an absence.

# ------------------------------------------------------------- session window
# The pass begins by reading the session it is closing. One page, ordered and
# bounded: an unordered prefix is not a page (cell-types.md, the two frozen
# properties of a read), and an unbounded select puts a whole table on a mailbox
# once a memory has been running for years.
if phase == "window":
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "episodes",
                    "columns": ["id", "session_id", "turn_id", "sender", "speaker",
                                "content", "happened_at", "recorded_at",
                                "channel", "audience_set", "mute_source"],
                    "where": {"session_id": session_id},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "recorded_at", "dir": "desc"},
                                 {"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}],
                    "limit": TURN_ROWS + PROOF}, "turns")])

if phase == "turns" and op == "select" and not err:
    emit([park_rows("turns", TURN_ROWS, "facts-read")])

# --------------------------------------------------------- the session's facts
# What the per-turn path already wrote for this session, WITH the record ids.
# Points 2, 3 and 4 of the contract are unobeyable without them: a model that
# cannot name a record can only rephrase it, and a rephrasing is exactly the
# restatement point 4 forbids. `expired_at is null` is the open set -- a row a
# dream run or a later turn already superseded is not what this session left
# standing, and offering it up would invite the pass to supersede it twice.
if phase == "facts-read" and op == "insert" and not err:
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "facts",
                    "columns": ["id", "episode_id", "subject", "canonical_subject",
                                "predicate", "canonical_predicate", "claim",
                                "canonical_claim", "fact_kind", "confidence",
                                "valid_from", "recorded_at", "source",
                                "audience_set", "muted_at", "mute_source",
                                "mute_words", "unmuted_at"],
                    "where": {"session_id": session_id,
                              "expired_at": {"is_null": True}},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "recorded_at", "dir": "desc"},
                                 {"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}],
                    "limit": FACT_ROWS + PROOF}, "facts-session")])

if phase == "facts-session" and op == "select" and not err:
    emit([park_rows("facts", FACT_ROWS, "topics-read")])

# ---------------------------------------------------------- the open topics
# `closed_at == ""` IS what open means in this table (the porter declared it
# without a null). Their ids travel for the same reason the facts' do: the pass
# may close a topic, and a topic it cannot name it cannot close.
#
# Bounded by TURN_ROWS rather than by a knob of its own, and the bound is not
# arbitrary: a topic is opened by a turn, so one session can hold at most as
# many topics as it has turns. The same argument bounds the exception list
# below. Two more knobs would be two more values to keep in agreement with this
# one for no reachable case.
if phase == "topics-read" and op == "insert" and not err:
    emit([store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "topics",
                    "columns": ["id", "name", "session_id", "opened_episode_id",
                                "opened_at", "channel", "audience_set"],
                    "where": {"session_id": session_id, "closed_at": ""},
                    "order_by": [{"col": "opened_at", "dir": "asc"},
                                 {"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}],
                    "limit": TURN_ROWS + PROOF}, "topics-open")])

if phase == "topics-open" and op == "select" and not err:
    emit([park_rows("topics", TURN_ROWS, "exceptions-read")])

# ------------------------------------------------------------ the exceptions
# The turns whose annotation never arrived. Since #298 this is no longer the
# pass's WORK list but its PRIORITY list: the prompt renders them first and says
# what they are, and an empty list -- the common case -- stays the health signal
# it always was. It gates nothing, which is why this read is emitted whether or
# not anything preceded it: a session with zero exceptions is the shape that
# used to be a skip, and a skip here would mean the pass never looked.
# The read itself leaves together with the mute reads (below, after the
# helpers it needs): one bundle, one park.


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- the meeting
# All four sets, read back under the one key: the join-less meeting point the
# prompt phase renders from. Ordered NEWEST first and bounded at MEET_ROWS, so
# that a session closed a second time reads its OWN sets and not the previous
# run's -- the phase that consumes this takes the FIRST row it sees per kind
# (`parked_set` below, and the reason is spelled out there).
def meet_op():
    return store_op({"operation": "select", "table": "scratch",
                     "columns": ["key", "kind", "payload", "created_at"],
                     "where": {"key": SCRATCH_KEY},
                     "order_by": [{"col": "created_at", "dir": "desc"},
                                  {"col": "kind", "dir": "asc"}],
                     "limit": MEET_ROWS}, "prompt")


def upgrade_report():
    """kfm M1c (review 5): the refused ops of the upgrade, said -- never a stop."""
    if not UPGRADE_REFUSED:
        return []
    codes = ",".join(sorted({str(r.get("error_code")) for r in UPGRADE_REFUSED}))
    return [{"header": {"route": "close_report", "phase": "mute-up",
                        "mute_up_refused": len(UPGRADE_REFUSED), "store_error": codes},
             "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "c-mute-up-report",
                           "text": "the close pass of session '%s' could not turn %d op(s)"
                                   " of an older store's closing requests into mutes (%s);"
                                   " those closures stand and the next pass tries again"
                                   % (session_id, len(UPGRADE_REFUSED), codes)}]}]


if phase == "meet" and op in ("insert", "bundle") and not err:
    emit([meet_op()] + upgrade_report())

# ------------------------------------------------------------- the four blocks
def parked_set(rows, kind):
    """One parked result set of THIS run, with its truncation flag.

    The FIRST row of a kind, never the last. The meeting read is ordered
    `created_at desc`, so the first row a kind has in that answer is the newest
    parking -- this run's. `insert` is not `upsert` and the key of this lane is
    the SESSION, so a session closed a second time parks four more rows beside
    the first four; the unordered "keep overwriting until the list ends" loop the
    ingress chain can afford (its key is a fresh batch id every time) would
    render the FIRST close of a session on its SECOND close, silently and with
    every id in it still resolvable.
    """
    for r in rows:
        if str(r.get("kind") or "") == kind:
            try:
                parcel = json.loads(r.get("payload") or "{}")
            except Exception:
                return [], False
            got = parcel.get("rows")
            return (got if isinstance(got, list) else []), bool(parcel.get("truncated"))
    return [], False


def parked_verdicts(rows):
    """The closer's answers of THIS run, one per group, read back out of the
    same meeting.

    GH #933: a run parks one verdict per group under the one session key, and a
    session closed a second time parks a second run of them beside the first.
    The run boundary is the rule `parked_set` already follows: the first `turns`
    row of the answer is this run's, so a verdict older than it belongs to an
    earlier run and is never acted on. Within the run the first row per group is
    the newest; an unreadable payload counts as no verdict for its group.
    """
    boundary = None
    for r in rows:
        if str(r.get("kind") or "") == "turns":
            boundary = str(r.get("created_at") or "")
            break
    if boundary is None:
        return {}
    out = {}
    for r in rows:
        if str(r.get("kind") or "") != "verdict":
            continue
        if str(r.get("created_at") or "") < boundary:
            continue
        try:
            parcel = json.loads(r.get("payload") or "{}")
        except Exception:
            continue
        if not isinstance(parcel, dict):
            continue
        try:
            g = int(parcel.get("close_group", 0))
        except Exception:
            continue
        out.setdefault(g, parcel)
    return out


def subject_key(f):
    """The IDENTITY of the entity a fact is about -- the store-owned canonical
    spelling, the written one as the fallback (byte-shared with `recall`,
    `extract-glue` and `dream-glue`)."""
    return f.get("canonical_subject") or f.get("subject")


def axis_key(f):
    """The IDENTITY of a fact's relation, same shape one dimension over."""
    return f.get("canonical_predicate") or f.get("predicate")


def statement_key(f):
    """The IDENTITY of the VALUE a fact states. Two assertions of one value are
    ONE statement, and the statement is what a `replaces` ends.

    GH #849: who stated it is part of the identity, the rule the chain helpers
    of recall and dream-glue follow -- a participant's claim and the member's own
    words are two statements, never one."""
    claim = f.get("canonical_claim") or f.get("claim")
    source = str(f.get("source") or "")
    if claim is None or not source:
        return claim
    return "%s says: %s" % (source, claim)


def open_axes(rows):
    """The open facts of this session as AXES of statements -- the ONE list.

    This is both halves of guard rail 3 at once: it is the block the prompt
    renders AND the `shown` array the write blocks carry, built by the same
    function out of the same rows. What the model was shown and what it may close
    are therefore one list BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by discipline -- the only
    way the two can never drift is that there is only one of them.

    The shape is the parked window's, byte for byte, because `extract-glue`'s
    apply phase reads it back that way: `subject` and `predicate` are the
    CANONICAL spellings (the closure echoes them in its `where`, on
    `canonical_subject`/`canonical_predicate`), an entry is the LAST assertion of
    a statement, and it carries two instants -- `since` is when the statement
    started, `last_asserted` is when it was said for the last time, which is the
    assertion a closure actually names and the one the direction guard compares
    against.
    """
    axes = {}
    for r in rows:
        if not (subject_key(r) and axis_key(r) and statement_key(r)):
            continue
        axes.setdefault((str(subject_key(r)), str(axis_key(r))), []).append(r)
    out = []
    for (subject, predicate) in sorted(axes):
        statements = {}
        for r in sorted(axes[(subject, predicate)],
                        key=lambda f: (str(f.get("valid_from") or ""),
                                       str(f.get("recorded_at") or ""),
                                       str(f.get("id") or ""))):
            statements.setdefault(str(statement_key(r)), []).append(r)
        items = [{"id": str(a[-1].get("id") or ""), "claim": str(a[-1].get("claim") or ""),
                  "since": str(a[0].get("valid_from") or ""),
                  "last_asserted": str(a[-1].get("valid_from") or "")}
                 for a in statements.values()]
        # GH #849: and WHO stated it, present only for a participant's claim, so
        # the window of a session without peers is byte for byte the old one and
        # the ingress can refuse a `replaces` that would cross sources.
        for item, a in zip(items, statements.values()):
            if str(a[-1].get("source") or ""):
                item["source"] = str(a[-1].get("source"))
        items.sort(key=lambda s: (s["since"], s["id"]))
        out.append({"subject": subject, "predicate": predicate, "statements": items})
    return out


def with_mutes(axis, record):
    """kfm M1c (review 7): the window an `extract-glue` batch checks a
    `replaces` against, with the mute of each muted statement -- the ingress
    gives the replacement the mute of what it replaces, so a sharpened or
    corrected muted fact does not come back unasked. A statement that is not
    muted is the window byte for byte; the closer's prompt renders the axes
    without it (open_axes)."""
    items = []
    for s in axis["statements"]:
        r = record.get(s["id"]) or {}
        if (str(r.get("muted_at") or "").strip()
                and not str(r.get("unmuted_at") or "").strip()):
            s = dict(s, mute={"muted_at": str(r.get("muted_at")),
                              "mute_source": str(r.get("mute_source") or ""),
                              "mute_words": str(r.get("mute_words") or "")})
        items.append(s)
    return dict(axis, statements=items)


def norm(value):
    """A COMPARISON key, and never a canonicalisation.

    Point 4 is checked by asking whether a proposal says what an open record of
    this session already says, and two models never spell one claim identically.
    Lower case with the punctuation squeezed out is enough for that question and
    is deliberately NOT enough for any other: `extract-glue`'s `predicate_key`
    stays the one place that rewrites a predicate, and the night's alias table
    stays the one place that decides two spellings are one relation. Nothing
    written here reaches a row.
    """
    return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-z]+", " ", str(value or "").lower()).strip()


def render_turns(turns, exceptions):
    """The session's turns, oldest first, the un-annotated ones in front.

    Two orders, two jobs, and they are not in conflict: the READ is newest-first
    so that a session longer than its page loses its oldest turns rather than its
    last ones, and the RENDERING is oldest-first because a conversation read
    backwards is a different conversation. This is where the page is turned
    around, exactly as task 15 said it would be.

    The turns whose annotation never arrived come FIRST and say so. That is the
    exception list being a PRIORITY rather than a fence (#298): the pass reads
    the whole session either way, and these are the turns least likely to have
    left a record behind.
    """
    missing = {str(r.get("episode_id") or "") for r in exceptions}
    missing.discard("")
    ordered = sorted(turns, key=lambda r: (str(r.get("happened_at")
                                               or r.get("recorded_at") or ""),
                                           str(r.get("id") or "")))

    def item(r, annotated):
        # GH #849: a peer's turn is marked the way the brain saw it on the wire,
        # `peer <ref>`, so the pass can tell another participant's words from
        # the member's own.
        speaker = str(r.get("speaker") or r.get("sender") or "")
        if str(r.get("sender") or "") == "peer":
            speaker = ("peer " + str(r.get("speaker"))) if r.get("speaker") else "peer"
        return {"episode_id": str(r.get("id") or ""),
                "speaker": speaker,
                "at": str(r.get("happened_at") or r.get("recorded_at") or ""),
                "text": str(r.get("content") or ""),
                "annotated": annotated}

    return ([item(r, False) for r in ordered if str(r.get("id") or "") in missing]
            + [item(r, True) for r in ordered if str(r.get("id") or "") not in missing])


def render_topics(topics):
    """The open topics WITH their ids -- a topic the pass cannot name it cannot
    close."""
    return [{"id": str(t.get("id") or ""), "name": str(t.get("name") or ""),
             "opened_episode_id": str(t.get("opened_episode_id") or ""),
             "opened_at": str(t.get("opened_at") or "")}
            for t in topics if t.get("id")]


def canon(aud):
    """The canonical participant set of one row, or None if it has none.

    GH #933: the close pass groups by the room a turn was recorded in, and two
    spellings of one set must be one room -- so the set is normalised exactly as
    `extract-glue`'s `audience_of` does it (deduplicated, blanks dropped,
    sorted). A missing, empty or unreadable value is NO audience, never an empty
    one: a turn without a room may not be shown to any room.
    """
    if isinstance(aud, list):
        items = aud
    else:
        if aud is None:
            return None
        try:
            items = json.loads(str(aud))
        except Exception:
            return None
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        return None
    out = sorted({str(x) for x in items if str(x)})
    return out or None


def groups(turns):
    """The turns of the window split into rounds: (groups, unaudienced).

    GH #933: one closer call sees ONE audience. A session can carry turns of
    several rooms, and a prompt over all of them would let a fact learned in one
    room be written for, corrected from or shown to another. A group is every
    turn of one canonical audience; `["*"]` is a room of its own and is never
    mixed in. Turns without an audience form no group at all -- they are only
    counted, so they never reach a prompt and are never a valid `episode_id`.
    The oldest group comes first, by its earliest turn in the key `render_turns`
    orders by, so the order of the closer calls follows the conversation.
    """
    by_audience = {}
    unaudienced = 0
    for r in turns:
        aud = canon(r.get("audience_set"))
        if aud is None:
            unaudienced += 1
            continue
        slot = by_audience.setdefault(json.dumps(aud), {"audience": aud, "turns": []})
        slot["turns"].append(r)

    def first(group):
        return min((str(r.get("happened_at") or r.get("recorded_at") or ""),
                    str(r.get("id") or "")) for r in group["turns"])

    return sorted(by_audience.values(), key=first), unaudienced


def facts_for(audience, facts):
    """The open facts one group may see: same canonical audience, nothing else.

    GH #933: equality, not a subset rule. A fact of a wider room names people
    this round may not hear about, a fact of a narrower one was said where this
    round was not -- and either one, once offered as a `sharpen` candidate, is a
    leak. A `*` fact therefore reaches only a `["*"]` group, a fact without an
    audience reaches none.
    """
    return [f for f in facts if canon(f.get("audience_set")) == audience]


def topics_for(audience, topics):
    """The open topics one group may see, by the rule `facts_for` follows: a
    topic name is content, and it leaks across rooms like any claim does."""
    return [t for t in topics if canon(t.get("audience_set")) == audience]

def confidence_of(raw, default=70):
    """A confidence on the 0-100 scale of the facts table. KD diagnosis
    (2026-10-06): the schema said `0`, models answered fractions, and
    `int(0.9)` filed every fact at 0 or 1 of 100. A float of at most 1 is read
    as a fraction; an integer is a percentage; anything unreadable is the
    default."""
    if isinstance(raw, bool):
        return default
    if isinstance(raw, str):
        try:
            raw = float(raw.strip())
        except ValueError:
            return default
        if raw.is_integer():
            raw = int(raw)
    if isinstance(raw, float):
        if raw != raw:
            return default
        if 0 <= raw <= 1:
            raw = raw * 100
        return max(0, min(100, int(round(raw))))
    if isinstance(raw, int):
        return max(0, min(100, raw))
    return default


def refuse_closer(text):
    """The pass has no verdict. Terminal, and it writes NOTHING.

    One reason for both ways of not having one -- the call failed, or the answer
    was not a verdict -- because the difference is in the sentence, not in what
    an operator does about it: no verdict means the session was not closed, and
    the priority list must NOT be swept, or the turns nobody annotated would be
    booked as looked at by a pass that never looked.
    """
    emit([{"header": {"route": "reject", "phase": "verdict",
                      "reject_reason": "closer_failed"},
           "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "c-reject",
                         "text": text}]}])


def ask_group(rounds, g, facts, topics, exceptions):

    of any other group (GH #933).

    `close_group` rides on the hop because a `code` cell sets no context: the
    edge to the closer promotes it, and from there it travels on every hop of
    the chain back to the apply phase, which is how that phase knows which
    group's verdict it just parked.

    group = rounds[g]
    emit([{"header": {"route": "close", "phase": "close", "close_group": str(g)},
           "system": {"instructions": {"text": INSTRUCTIONS}},
           "messages": [{"origin": "user", "type": "text", "id": "c-ask",

NAME_CHARS = 64

FORGET_WORDS = 4

# `forget_fallback` is on -- since the mute semantics the default (a mute is
# undone by one turn and hides nothing from a question, so the 7 of 10

# line, null or a typo keep it). Off (false, 0) the pass honours the requests
# the closer cites and nothing else, each still checked against the turn's

FORGET_FALLBACK = _flag("forget_fallback", True)
# GH #1074: the closer emitted `forget` for 3 of 10 member turns that asked in
# so many words (a six-month boundary run, 10 forget probes); the other 7 got
# `"forget": []` and the secret stayed in every bundle. So a member turn whose
# OWN sentence asks is a request whether the closer names it or not, and the
# words come from that sentence. Narrower than the cues on purpose, because
# no model read the turn: the verb has to be addressed to the memory (sentence
# start, after "please", "can you", "I want you to") and name a thing ("forget
# what / that / about / the ..."). "I always forget my keys" is a statement,
# "forget it" names nothing; both ask for nothing.
#
# Review K2-R8 (C1/I1/I3) and the coordinator's rule of 07.10.: a request is a
# sentence of its OWN, read as one small grammar --
#     [address ,] [frame] [please] VERB [please] THING ...
# -- the imperative of the verb addressed to the memory, naming a thing. The
# address is one or two words before a comma ("Hey Lumo, "); the frame is the
# polite question that IS an imperative ("can/could you", "I want you to").

# where the grammar says so (the German fixture cases `reminder`, review C1:
# such a sentence asks to KEEP the thing, and was read as a request to forget it).
ASK_ADDRESS = r"^(?:[^\W\d_]+(?:\s+[^\W\d_]+)?\s*,\s*)?"
FORGET_ASKS = tuple(
    (ASK_ADDRESS + str(a.get("pattern") or "").replace("{thing}", str(block.get("thing") or "")),
     bool(a.get("reminder")), code)
    for code, block in LANGS for a in (block.get("asks") or [])
    if isinstance(a, dict) and a.get("pattern"))
ASK_NEGATION = {code: str(block.get("negation") or "") for code, block in LANGS}
ASK_TOLD = {code: str(block.get("told") or "") for code, block in LANGS}
# A name or a tag after the last comma ("..., Lumo." / "..., okay?") is
# addressed, it is no part of the thing.
ASK_TAIL = r",\s*[^\W\d_]+\s*[.!?]*\s*$"
# Review D1 (kf89 deep review): the correction idiom is no request to forget
# the NEW value. "Forget what I said, the appointment is on Tuesday." took its
# words from the whole rest of the sentence -- the new value included -- and
# `forget-o` then marked exactly the corrected fact of the same turn. A comma
# or semicolon followed by at least CONTINUATION_WORDS words ends the thing:
# its words come only from before it, and a continued request reaches neither
# the facts of its own turn (`forget-o`) nor its own episode, which carries
# the new value. A grammar count of words, no content bound. Review KF-F
# (F1): three let "Vergiss das, Dienstag passt." through with the new value as
# the thing; with the one-word tail gone first (ASK_TAIL), one word after the
# comma already continues the sentence.
CONTINUATION_WORDS = 1
ASK_CONJUNCTION = {code: str(block.get("conjunction") or "") for code, block in LANGS}
# One-word list items after a comma, the last one led by the conjunction
# (", Ben, and Carl." / ", Ben und Carl." / ", and Carl.").
LIST_TAIL = (r"\s*(?:[^\W\d_]+(?:\s*,\s*[^\W\d_]+)*\s*,?\s+)?(?:%s)\s+[^\W\d_]+"
             r"\s*[.!?]*\s*")
# Page of the `peer <ref>` bindings a name is checked against before it binds.
ALIAS_ROWS = 512


def turn_source(row):
    """The source a turn's facts carry: a peer's reference, "" for the own side."""
    if str(row.get("sender") or "") == "peer":
        return str(row.get("speaker") or "") or None
    return ""


def clean_name(raw, ref):
    """A participant's name fit to be a canonical subject, or ""."""
    if not isinstance(raw, str):
        return ""
    name = " ".join(raw.split())
    if (not name or len(name) > NAME_CHARS or name.lower() in (ref, "peer " + ref)
            or any(c in name for c in "[]{}<>|") or not re.search(r"[^\W\d_]", name)):
        return ""
    return name


def forget_words(words, least=2):
    """The distinct words of a request that can narrow a search: three letters
    or more, none of FORGET_STOPWORDS, at most FORGET_WORDS. Fewer than two is
    no search at all -- one word, or filler, would match half a life. Review
    K2-R8 I3: the member's own sentence may name its thing in one (`least`
    1)."""
    if not isinstance(words, str):
        return []
    stop = set(FORGET_STOPWORDS)
    found = []
    for w in re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]{3,}", words.lower()):
        if w not in stop and w not in found:
            found.append(w)
    return found[:FORGET_WORDS] if len(found) >= max(1, least) else []


def match_of(words, column="", least=2, joiner=" AND "):
    """An FTS5 expression that needs EVERY word: quoted, so no word is syntax.
    `column` narrows each phrase to one indexed column (`claim : "w"`);
    `joiner` " OR " needs any one of them."""
    found = forget_words(words, least)
    pre = column + " : " if column else ""
    return joiner.join('%s"%s"' % (pre, w) for w in found)


def request_parts(text):
    """GH #1074: the words of a member turn's own request to forget, whether
    the asking sentence goes on past its thing, and whether its verb may be
    honoured without the closer citing it (FALLBACK_VERBS) -- ("", False,
    False) where it asks nothing. The first sentence that asks (FORGET_ASKS, the grammar above)
    gives them. Review K2-R8 I2: only the text AFTER the asking words counts --
    "Could you", "Hey Lumo," or what the member did first is no part of the
    thing, and in an AND search one such word missed the secret. Review D1: a
    continuation clause (thing_cut: words after a comma or semicolon)
    ends the thing -- "Forget what I said, the appointment is on Tuesday." names
    no thing at all, and the new value is never a word of the request. Then the
    same narrowing as a closer's words (forget_words), one word only where the
    sentence says it was told (the language's `told`)."""
    for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?;])\s+|\n+", str(text or "")):
        body = sentence.strip()
        for pattern, reminder, code in FORGET_ASKS:
            m = re.search(pattern, body, re.IGNORECASE)
            if not m:
                continue
            if reminder and asks_to_keep(body, m, code):
                break
            rest, continued = thing_cut(body[m.end():], code)
            found = forget_words(rest, 1)
            told = ASK_TOLD.get(code) or ""
            if len(found) == 1 and not (told and re.search(told, body[:m.end()] + rest,
                                                           re.IGNORECASE)):
                found = []
            verb = m.group("verb") if "verb" in m.re.groupindex else None
            allowed = FALLBACK_VERBS.get(code) or ""
            fallback = verb is None or bool(
                allowed and re.fullmatch(allowed, " ".join(verb.lower().split()), re.IGNORECASE))
            return " ".join(found), continued and bool(found), fallback
    return "", False, False


def request_words(text):
    """The words of request_parts alone."""
    return request_parts(text)[0]


def continues(text):
    """Review D1: whether the asking sentence of a turn goes on past its thing
    -- for a request the closer cited as much as for one read here."""
    for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?;])\s+|\n+", str(text or "")):
        body = sentence.strip()
        for pattern, _reminder, code in FORGET_ASKS:
            m = re.search(pattern, body, re.IGNORECASE)
            if m:
                return thing_cut(body[m.end():], code)[1]
    return False


def thing_cut(rest, code):
    """The thing of an asking sentence -- the text after its asking words --
    and whether the sentence goes on past it. Review KF-F (F1): a one-word
    tail after the last comma is addressed (ASK_TAIL) and dropped; after that
    EVERY comma or semicolon followed by CONTINUATION_WORDS words ends the
    thing -- "Forget that, Tuesday works." and "Vergiss das mit Montag,
    Dienstag passt." go on with the new value in two words, and those two
    words are never the thing. One shape does not end it: a list of one-word
    items whose last one follows the language's `conjunction` ("Anna, Ben,
    and Carl") is the thing itself."""
    rest = re.sub(ASK_TAIL, "", rest)
    conj = ASK_CONJUNCTION.get(code) or ""
    for cut in re.finditer(r"[,;]", rest):
        after = rest[cut.end():]
        if conj and re.fullmatch(LIST_TAIL % conj, after, re.IGNORECASE):
            break
        if len(re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]+", after)) >= CONTINUATION_WORDS:
            return rest[:cut.start()], True
    return rest, False


def asks_to_keep(body, m, code):
    """Review K2-R8 C1: an imperative with a negation of its language in its own
    clause or as the sentence's last word is a reminder."""
    negation = ASK_NEGATION.get(code) or ""
    if not negation:
        return False
    clause = body[m.start("verb"):].split(",", 1)[0] if "verb" in m.re.groupindex else body
    last = re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]+", body)[-1:]
    return bool(re.search(negation, clause, re.IGNORECASE)
                or (last and re.fullmatch(negation, last[0], re.IGNORECASE)))


def forget_phase(kind, request, at, words):
    """`forget-<kind>|<request turn>|<time asked>|<word,word>`: a code cell
    holds no state between hops, so the mark the answer writes (who asked,
    when, about what) travels with the search. Words are letters only, the
    time an ISO stamp -- neither carries a `|` or a `,`."""
    return "forget-%s|%s|%s|%s" % (kind, request, at, ",".join(words))


def forget_phase_parts(phase):
    """The request turn, the time it asked and its words, of a `forget-*`
    phase (an older two-part phase reads as no time and no words)."""
    parts = phase.split("|")
    request = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    at = parts[2] if len(parts) > 2 and not parts[2].isdigit() else ""
    words = [w for w in (parts[3] if len(parts) > 3 else "").split(",") if w]
    return request, at, words


def forget_searches(episode_id, words, until, cover, least=2, earlier=(), continued=False):
    """The searches of one request (#1039 review B2): facts by their claim
    text, episodes by their content, bounded by the request's own time and by
    nothing else (R-TR-25: a mute may be broad). GH #1074: the facts' window
    is `valid_from`, the time the fact holds from -- the clock `happened_at` is
    on. `recorded_at` is the write clock: a fact extracted later from an older
    turn, or an imported history, is never `<=` the request, and the boundary
    run found no fact by this search in 3 of 3 honoured requests.

    Review K2-R8:
    - M1: a fact of a LATER turn of the request's own session can hold from a
      time before it ("the bank debt from 2020 is paid off now", five minutes
      after the request). So the fact search splits: other sessions by
      `valid_from` (`forget-f`), this session only from the turns up to the
      request, `earlier` (`forget-s`) -- the store has `in`, no `not in`.
    - I4: only the speaker's own facts (`source` ""), never a peer's; and of
      the request's own turn only the facts whose claim carries one of the
      words (`forget-o`) -- "My daughter's birthday is June 3." said in the
      same turn stays.

    Review D1 (kf89 deep review): `forget-o` needs EVERY word of the request
    (it took any one of them and so the corrected fact of "Forget what I said,
    the appointment is on Tuesday."), and a `continued` request -- the asking
    sentence goes on past its thing -- reaches neither its own turn's facts
    nor its own episode: what follows the comma is new, not forgotten.
    Review N3: the episode search reaches the own side only (`sender` not
    `peer`, the same line `turn_source` draws for the facts' `source`): a
    peer's episode in a shared room that happens to carry every word stays."""
    found = forget_words(words, least)
    if not found:
        return []
    fact_expr = match_of(words, "claim", least)
    expr = match_of(words, "", least)
    own = {"audience_set": {"covers": cover}, "source": {"or_null": {"eq": ""}},
           "expired_at": {"or_null": {"eq": ""}}}
    ops = [store_op({"operation": "search", "table": "facts",
                     "match": fact_expr, "columns": ["id"],
                     "where": dict(own, valid_from={"lte": until},
                                   session_id={"or_null": {"neq": session_id}})},
                    forget_phase("f", episode_id, until, found))]
    if earlier:
        ops.append(store_op({"operation": "search", "table": "facts",
                             "match": fact_expr, "columns": ["id"],
                             "where": dict(own, episode_id={"in": sorted(set(earlier))})},
                            forget_phase("s", episode_id, until, found)))
    if not continued:
        ops.append(store_op({"operation": "search", "table": "facts",
                             "match": fact_expr, "columns": ["id"],
                             "where": dict(own, episode_id={"eq": episode_id})},
                            forget_phase("o", episode_id, until, found)))
    episodes = {"audience_set": {"covers": cover}, "happened_at": {"lte": until},
                "sender": {"or_null": {"neq": "peer"}}}
    if continued:
        episodes["id"] = {"neq": episode_id}
    ops.append(store_op({"operation": "search", "table": "episodes",
                         "match": expr, "columns": ["id"], "where": episodes},
                        forget_phase("e", episode_id, until, found)))
    return ops


def asks_to_forget(text):
    """Whether a turn's own text carries a forget cue (FORGET_CUES) in a
    sentence that is no reminder (FORGET_REMINDS, review K2-R8 C1): "Don't
    forget my birthday" or a negated German imperative ask to keep a thing,
    and a closer that cites one is not taken at its word."""
    for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?;])\s+|\n+", str(text or "")):
        if (any(re.search(c, sentence, re.IGNORECASE)
                for c in FORGET_CUES + FORGET_KEEPS_MUTED)
                and not any(re.search(r, sentence, re.IGNORECASE) for r in FORGET_REMINDS)):
            return True
    return False


def forget_report(request, kind, muted=0, mute_unmatched=0):
    """Review N2 (kf89 deep review): a request counts where its rows are MARKED,
    not where its search was sent. Each search answer reports itself, one hop
    after the close report: how many rows it muted, or that it found nothing.
    `search` is the phase letter (f, s, o, e; p = provenance). R-TR-25: the
    closing report fields (`forgotten`, `forget_too_broad`, `forget_unmatched`)
    are gone with the closing semantics -- nothing is forgotten and nothing is
    too broad to mute -- and `muted` / `mute_unmatched` say what happened."""
    text = ("forget request %s, search %s: muted %d row(s)" % (request, kind, muted)
            if muted else
            "forget request %s, search %s: nothing found" % (request, kind))
    return {"header": {"route": "close_report", "phase": "forget", "request": request,
                       "search": kind, "muted": muted, "mute_unmatched": mute_unmatched},
            "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "c-forget-report",
                          "text": text}]}


def mute_set(mark, at, words):
    """The columns a mute writes (R-TR-25). `unmuted_at` is cleared, so a topic
    the member put aside a second time after taking it up is muted again."""
    return {"muted_at": at or now, "mute_source": mark,
            "mute_words": " ".join(words), "unmuted_at": ""}


def forget_beliefs(fact_ids, mark, at, words):
    """GH #1039 review B3: a belief the night derived from a muted fact carries
    the same mute, one update per fact (a belief names its facts in
    `source_fact_ids`, and `covers` is membership). `active` and
    `closure_source` are not touched."""
    return [store_op({"operation": "update", "table": "beliefs",
                      "set": mute_set(mark, at, words),
                      "where": {"source_fact_ids": {"covers": [f]}}},
                     "forget-b")
            for f in sorted(set(fact_ids))]


def alias_norm(value):
    """A comparison key for an alias-table spelling: case fold, NFC, collapsed
    whitespace. Stricter than the store's own normal form only in composing
    more marks -- which can refuse a binding, never let a colliding one by."""
    import unicodedata
    return " ".join(unicodedata.normalize("NFC", str(value or "")).lower().split())


def says_name(text, name):
    """GH #1039 review N1: whether a turn's text carries the name -- the whole
    name as a run of words (alias_norm on both sides), or else every word of
    it with three letters or more. A fragment of a word is no name."""
    words = re.findall(r"\w+", alias_norm(text))
    parts = re.findall(r"\w+", alias_norm(name))
    if not parts:
        return False
    n = len(parts)
    if any(words[i:i + n] == parts for i in range(len(words) - n + 1)):
        return True
    long_parts = [w for w in parts if len(w) >= 3]
    return bool(long_parts) and all(w in words for w in long_parts)


def forget_update(table, ids, mark, at, words):
    """Mute rows (R-TR-25). Never `closed_at`, `expired_at` or `closure_source`:
    a muted row is open, it is only not raised unasked. A row muted before by
    another request is muted by this one now -- the newest request owns it, and
    lifting the older one no longer reaches it."""
    return store_op({"operation": "update", "table": table,
                     "set": mute_set(mark, at, words),
                     "where": {"id": {"in": sorted(set(ids))}}},
                    "muted")


def topic_words(text):
    """The words of a turn the way a request's words are kept: three letters or
    more, case folded (forget_words without the stopwords and the bound)."""
    return set(re.findall(r"[^\W\d_]{3,}", str(text or "").lower()))


def names_word(word, asked):
    """Whether a set of asked words carries one word of a mute: the word
    itself or the same word inflected. The request said "owes", the question
    says "owe"; "neighbours". kfm M1c (review 3): two words are one
    where they share a prefix of max(4, the shorter one less two) letters
    ("repaid" / "repaying"; "owed" / "owing" no), a short word of five
    letters or fewer all of it but its last ("owed" / "owes", "owe" / "owes"),
    and never fewer than three ("own" is no "owe"). Deterministic and blind
    to the language."""
    if word in asked:
        return True
    for a in asked:
        short = min(len(a), len(word))
        need = max(3, short - 1) if short <= 5 else max(4, short - 2)
        common = 0
        for x, y in zip(a, word):
            if x != y:
                break
            common += 1
        if common >= need:
            return True
    return False


def takes_up(words, at, request, turns):
    """R-TR-25: whether the member takes a muted topic up again -- a turn of
    their OWN (`sender` user) after the request, not itself asking to forget,
    that carries every word of the thing (names_word). "You can talk about the money my
    neighbour owes me again" is such a turn as much as "Did my neighbour pay
    back the money he owes me?" -- the member names the topic, so it is theirs
    to talk about again. The turn ids it was found in, or None."""
    need = set(words)
    if not need:
        return None
    last = {}
    for t in turns:
        before, last = last, t
        tid = str(t.get("id") or "")
        when = str(t.get("happened_at") or t.get("recorded_at") or "")
        if (not tid or tid == request or str(t.get("sender") or "") != "user"
                or not when or not at or when <= at):
            continue
        # kfm M1c (review 1): asking to forget it, or to keep it aside
        # (`keeps_muted`), or saying yes to the other side's question about
        # which topic was meant, names the topic without taking it up.
        if asks_to_forget(t.get("content")):
            continue
        if (str(before.get("sender") or "") not in ("", "user")
                and "?" in str(before.get("content") or "")
                and any(re.search(a, str(t.get("content") or ""), re.IGNORECASE)
                        for a in FORGET_AFFIRMS)):
            continue
        said = topic_words(t.get("content"))
        if all(names_word(w, said) for w in need):
            return tid
    return None


def unmute(mark):
    """Lift one mute, on every table it reached. `muted_at` stays as the record
    of when it was set; `unmuted_at` is what ends it."""
    return [store_op({"operation": "update", "table": table,
                      "set": {"unmuted_at": now},
                      "where": {"mute_source": mark, "unmuted_at": {"or_null": {"eq": ""}}}},
                     "unmuted")
            for table in ("episodes", "facts", "beliefs")]


# R-TR-25, the upgrade from the closing semantics. `closure_source` has no
# prefix operator, and a store predicate carries ONE operator per column (a
# `gte` + `lt` range is refused, and a refused read ends the lane with no
# report -- kfm M1b, gh933: every pass hung). Ordered by `closure_source`
# from `forget_request:` on, the request closures are the head of the page;
# legacy_mutes keeps only those.
LEGACY_RANGE = {"gte": FORGET_SOURCE}


def legacy_read(table, columns):
    return {"operation": "select", "table": table, "columns": columns,
            "where": {"closure_source": LEGACY_RANGE},
            "order_by": [{"col": "closure_source", "dir": "asc"},
                         {"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}],
            "limit": TURN_ROWS}


def legacy_mutes(rows):
    """One mute per closing request the read found: its words from the request
    turn itself where that turn is among the rows (the episode search of a
    request reached its own turn), else the words its closed turns share; the
    time from that turn or the closure."""
    found = {}
    for r in rows:
        if not isinstance(r, dict):
            continue
        mark = str(r.get("closure_source") or "")
        if not mark.startswith(FORGET_SOURCE):
            continue
        entry = found.setdefault(mark, {"at": "", "words": [], "own": False, "seen": []})
        if str(r.get("id") or "") == mark[len(FORGET_SOURCE):]:
            entry["words"] = request_words(r.get("content")).split()
            entry["at"] = str(r.get("happened_at") or "")
            entry["own"] = True
        entry["seen"].append(topic_words(r.get("content")) - set(FORGET_STOPWORDS))
        if not entry["at"]:
            entry["at"] = str(r.get("closed_at") or r.get("expired_at") or "")
    # kfm M1c (review 4): the request turn may lie beyond the page (a request
    # that closed more turns than a page holds) or be no row of its own (a
    # continued request). Every episode the request closed carried all of its
    # words -- the search was an AND -- so the words its closed turns on this
    # page share are the thing, or hold it; a mute never goes without words.
    for entry in found.values():
        if not entry["own"] and entry["seen"]:
            first, rest = entry["seen"][0], entry["seen"][1:]
            entry["words"] = sorted(w for w in first
                                    if all(names_word(w, other) for other in rest))
        del entry["own"], entry["seen"]
    return found


def legacy_turn(mark, at, words, tables):
    """The writes that make one closing request a mute: the closure undone
    (`closure_source` "", and the `closed_at` / `expired_at` the request set),
    the mute set. Only rows whose author is this request -- every other
    closure keeps its own."""
    ends = {"episodes": "closed_at", "facts": "expired_at", "beliefs": None}
    ops = []
    for table in tables:
        change = dict(mute_set(mark, at, words), closure_source="")
        if ends[table]:
            # NULL, not "": an open fact is `expired_at is null` to every
            # reader of this hive (the session read above among them).
            change[ends[table]] = None
        ops.append({"operation": "update", "table": table, "set": change,
                    "where": {"closure_source": mark}})
    return ops
